what_this_is: One de-duplicated list of the defects and design limitations found by the audit, each checked by a skeptic pass. The dashboard is a portfolio demo on fictional data (Example Ranch); it is not production-ready, and this list is not a claim that fixing it makes it so. Each entry's 'verifier' field holds the verified finding and its evidence; 'proposed_fix' and 'phase' are recommendations; open assumptions are listed in 'unresolved_assumptions'. Research conclusions (research_*.json, cite_*.json) are not part of this registry.

status.confirmed: Reproduced and accepted as a defect by the skeptic pass (partially-confirmed verdicts are kept as confirmed with the narrowed scope stated in 'status_note' or 'verifier'). Four baseline-only entries (UI-02, UI-03, UI-12, UI-13) had no skeptic review; they are marked confirmed because the measurement was reproduced, and each says so in 'status_note'.
status.design-limitation: Reproduced, but the code does what its documented rule says; the gap is in the rule set or data model.
status.plausible: Observed but a judgement call that no skeptic reviewed (baseline only).

severity.high: Likely with ordinary data or a routine change (a common export shape, a blank or mistyped cell, a renamed group, a missing file), and it hides a whole area or a critical alert with no sign, raises a false critical alarm from a common data slip, or blanks or freezes the page.
severity.medium: Hides, invents or distorts an alert under a narrower or less common trigger (a reading gap, a viewer in another time zone, a back-dated as_of, one mistyped cell), or is visibly wrong or misleading; also rule-design gaps with a real operational or credibility cost.
severity.low: Cosmetic or wording, a rare edge or boundary case, or a gap where the alert itself stays visible.

phase.1: Fix now: data reading and contract, the three states (OK / needs attention / CAN'T TELL), loading and errors, one as-of policy, rule fixes, safe rendering, honest rule copy.
phase.2: Build next: morning review, filters, alert explanations, freshness and coverage strip, keyboard and touch chart access, phone tables, printable crew briefing, rest checks, consequence-aware ranking, optional per-device notes.
phase.3: At most three additions: water supply coverage from capacity and head count; forage observations at moves; a dated drought or precipitation snapshot.
phase.defer: Out of the planned phases (needs a model or integration beyond them).

effort.S: Small: a focused change, usually under a day.

definitions.demo_settings: Every threshold in the rules is a demo setting chosen for the fictional example, not a validated value: tank 25% critical / 40% low, 30-point drop in 24 hours, 24 hours of sensor silence, planned graze days per pasture, 2-day move grace, gain 80% / 50% of target, 2.0 / 1.0 lb daily gain targets, health tasks due within 7 days, budget 5% / 10% over. Any new setting proposed here is also a demo setting.
definitions.data: All ranch data in the repository is fictional (Example Ranch). Health entries cover observation, scheduling, records and escalation to a veterinarian only.

policies.severity: Severity is the skeptic-endorsed severity after explicit corrections. For merged entries the highest verified severity is used unless a skeptic explicitly lowered it. High stands for a 404 or aborted request on pastures, moves, weights, water or meta. Baseline B1 (not skeptic-reviewed) graded the blank-skeleton state medium; the registry takes the verified high. That the GitHub Pages 404 page behaves the same is an inference (the proxy refused the site). findings.proposed_fix: Put a 'Loading example data...' placeholder in index.html. Wrap loading in try/catch and collect per-file failures into a banner at the top. Run each area's rules and each section's render in its own try/catch; a failed area becomes a visible "CAN'T TELL: water data unavailable (<reason>)" row instead of throwing. A missing or empty meta.csv is a fatal error with its own message.

findings.title: Dates and times are never validated or parsed once: day-first, impossible, numeric, space-separated or M/D/YYYY values silently drop alerts, invent alerts or crash
findings.verifier: confirmed (verify_time F1, F5, F6; verify_gain F9; verify_healthbudget F13), partially-confirmed (verify_csv F14, verify_water F3), plus the health/budget skeptic's own missed finding M1. Evidence: TIME-07 '(no alert)' for a due date of 15/09/2026; TIME-08 'Day 113 of a 21-day plan (92 days over)'; TIME-19 '6 rows ... missing: T6, Yearlings in Sand Hills, Booster, Pinkeye'; CSV-39 'Due in 1 day (2026-09-31)'; health M2 case 'Overdue by 20725.99946380787 days (due 46327)'. Corrections applied: that an Excel re-save turns 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM' into M/D/YYYY is unverified (no Excel was run); the realistic triggers are date-only columns re-saved by a spreadsheet, space-separated ISO timestamps, hand-typed rows and typos. M/D/YYYY fails visibly with fractions in US zones rather than silently, and a whole water file in M/D form is loud (8 silent tanks), which the water skeptic graded medium; day-first weigh dates make every ADG NaN (gain.missed M6); a day-first as_of shows 'Data as of Invalid Date.' High stands for the silent loss of an overdue health task and the silent drops from typos. Registrar re-ran TIME-07/08/09/19, W-05/W-05b and gain.missed M6 on 2026-10-16: same.
findings.location: exceptions.js:36 (days() uses new Date on raw strings), :43 and :68 (string localeCompare sort), :48, :58, :95, :142; exceptions.js:30 (number-looking dates become Numbers); app.js:113, :223
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/time.repro.mjs (CASE TIME-05, TIME-06, TIME-07, TIME-08, TIME-09, TIME-10, TIME-19); node docs/audit/diagnostics/csv.repro.mjs (CASE CSV-38..CSV-42, CSV-40b); node docs/audit/diagnostics/water.repro.mjs (CASE W-05: newest row written '2026-09-30 18:00'; W-05b); node docs/audit/diagnostics/gain.repro.mjs (CASE GN-16); node docs/audit/diagnostics/gain.missed.mjs (CASE M6: day-first weigh dates); node docs/audit/diagnostics/healthbudget.repro.mjs (CASE H-08, run with TZ=America/Chicago and TZ=Europe/Berlin); node docs/audit/diagnostics/healthbudget.skeptic.missed.mjs (CASE M2: next_due 46327); node docs/audit/diagnostics/time.verify.mjs (CASE F7+); node docs/audit/diagnostics/csv.verify.mjs (CASE CV-06); node docs/audit/diagnostics/time.browser.mjs (CASE TB-09). Minimal input: health row 'Yearlings,Booster vaccine,2026-06-02,15/09/2026,open' with as_of 2026-09-30T18:00.
findings.expected: Each date column accepts one documented form (YYYY-MM-DD for days; YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM for timestamps, read in the ranch zone, TIME-02). Anything else, including '2026-09-31', '15/09/2026', '46327' and '2026-13-01', becomes a visible data issue naming the file, row and value, and is never judged silently. Valid data gives whole-day counts for every viewer: booster 'Overdue by 15 days' (Sep 15 to Sep 30); Sand Hills 'Day 24 of a 21-day plan (3 days over)'; the newest water reading is chosen by parsed time.
findings.actual: TIME-07: '(no alert)'. TIME-08: 'serious: Yearlings in Sand Hills: Day 113 of a 21-day plan (92 days over)'. TIME-09: 'silentHours=NaN; (no alert)'. TIME-19: '6 rows (critical 2, serious 3, warning 1); missing: T6, Yearlings in Sand Hills, Booster, Pinkeye'; TB-09 header 'Data as of Invalid Date.'. CSV-39: 'warning|Cows: Pinkeye check|Due in 1 day (2026-09-31)'. TIME-05 (Chicago): 'Day 21.791666666666668 of a 21-day plan (0.7916666666666679 days over)'. W-05: 'sorted order=2026-09-29T18:00 , 2026-09-30 18:00 , 2026-09-30T12:00; level used=75; (no water alerts)'. GN-16 compact dates: 'threw TypeError: a.date.localeCompare is not a function'. gain M6: 'Heifers adg=NaN ... rows=[]; total exceptions=8'. Health M2: 'serious | Yearlings: Deworm | Overdue by 20725.99946380787 days (due 46327)'. H-08 (Berlin): 'serious | Cows: Pinkeye check | Overdue by 0.08333333333333333 days'.
findings.consequence: Spreadsheet re-saves, hand-typed rows and database exports change date formats. When that happens an overdue booster, an overstay or a dead sensor can disappear while the shorter list still looks complete; a day-first move date raises a false '92 days over'; spreadsheet serial dates turn open health tasks into 'Overdue by 20725 days'; a space-separated newest reading hides a tank at 20%.
findings.regression_test: For each date column, feed '15/09/2026', '2026-09-31', '2026-13-01', '46327' and '' (where a date is required): findExceptions returns a data issue row naming the file and value, and never silently returns fewer rows. Valid committed data: 10 rows. Water rows 2026-09-30T06:00 50, 2026-09-30T12:00 49 and '2026-09-30 18:00' 20 with as_of 2026-09-30T18:00: a data issue for the space form or, if that form is accepted, critical 'Down to 20% full'. Under TZ=America/Chicago and TZ=Pacific/Auckland every Grazing and Health problem matches /\b\d+ days?\b/ with no decimal point. Health next_due 46327: no 'Overdue' row (spreadsheet serial 46327 is 2026-11-01, 32 days after Sep 30).
findings.proposed_fix: Strict parsers in the data contract: parseDay accepts only /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/ and checks that the day exists (round trip through Date.UTC); parseStamp accepts YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM (optionally with an offset) and reads it in the ranch zone (TIME-02). Parse once at load into numbers, sort numerically, count whole days from Date.UTC parts, and report anything else as a data issue with file, row and value. Date columns are never turned into numbers.

findings.title: Duplicate and contradictory records are not detected: re-exported budget rows, a pasture listed twice, repeated health tasks or groups double or distort alerts
findings.verifier: confirmed (verify_csv F13). Evidence: CSV-33 'warning|Fuel|7% over season to date' where the de-duplicated figures (9,600 and 10,000) give 4.2%, under the 5% demo warning line; the committed budget.csv appended to itself gives 'NEW serious|Budget|Fuel|21% over season to date ($4,080)' and Repairs '$3,600'; CSV-35 prints the booster row twice. Related duplicate cases with their own entries: two open moves for one group (GRZ-02), two readings at one timestamp (WAT-07), a same-day weigh-in (GAIN-02).
findings.location: exceptions.js:55 (the last duplicate pasture wins), :84-87 (budget rows summed blindly), :97, :140-147 (each health row judged), :56 (several open moves per group allowed)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/csv.repro.mjs (CASE CSV-33..CSV-37). Minimal input: the committed budget.csv with its data rows appended a second time.
findings.expected: Duplicate keys are detected and shown as data issue rows; exact duplicates are dropped and counted. CSV-33: no alerts, or one duplicate data issue. CSV-35 and CSV-36: one alert each. Doubled budget: Fuel still '$2,040', not '$4,080'.
findings.actual: CSV-33: 'warning|Fuel|7% over season to date'. CSV-34 (pasture listed twice): '(no alerts)'. CSV-35: two identical 'serious|Yearlings: Booster vaccine|Overdue by 15 days' rows. CSV-36: two identical Heifers rows. Doubled budget: 'serious|Budget|Fuel|21% over season to date ($4,080)' and Repairs '$3,600'.
findings.consequence: A re-export or a block pasted twice creates false budget warnings and doubles dollar figures; repeated health rows inflate the 'Needs attention' count; a pasture listed twice is judged against whichever plan comes last.
findings.regression_test: CSV-33 fixture: no alerts, or one duplicate data issue. Committed budget.csv appended to itself: Fuel '21% over season to date ($2,040)' (11,640 - 9,600) plus a duplicate note. CSV-35 fixture: exactly one booster row.
findings.proposed_fix: Key uniqueness per file in the data contract: pasture_id, group, tank_id, (month, category), (group, task, next_due), (tank_id, time), (tag, date), and at most one open move per group. Exact duplicates are dropped and counted; conflicting duplicates become data issue rows.

findings.verifier: confirmed (verify_time F3, verify_water F6, verify_gain F15). Evidence: W-07 'T6 silentHours=-678' and T6's serious row disappears; TIME-11 'T6 silentHours=-6; (no T6 alert)'; GN-12 'serious | Heifers | 0.45 lbs/day since 2026-09-15'. Corrections applied: TIME-11 does not make a dead sensor read as fresh (T6 really reported again); the defect is an inconsistent report under a Sep 30 header. The stronger repro is a back-dated as_of: the committed data with as_of 2026-09-15T18:00 shows the T2 and T4 critical alerts that only happened Sep 26-30 and 'Heifers here now' at Lone Tree before they arrived (time.verify F4+). W-07: T6 still serious 'No reading for 42 hours; last level 98.5%' (Sep 29 00:00 to Sep 30 18:00 = 42 h). GN-12: '0.44 lbs/day since 2026-07-20'. As of 2026-09-15T18:00 the committed data gives no water alerts (T2's fall starts Sep 26, the T4 leak Sep 29).
findings.actual: W-07: 'T6 silentHours=-678; critical | Tank T2 (Windmill) | Down to 11.8% full || critical | Tank T4 (Lone Tree, Heifers here now) | Dropped 46 points in 24 hours, now 10%' (T6 gone). W-06: 'silentHours=-48; (no water alerts)'. B-04: the last-point dot at cx=319.14, past the plot edge at 254. F4+: 'critical: Tank T2 (Windmill): Down to 11.8% full / critical: Tank T4 (Lone Tree, Heifers here now): Dropped 46 points in 24 hours, now 10%' with T2/T4 silentHours = -360. GN-12: 'Heifers from=2026-09-15 to=2026-10-15  ||  serious | Heifers | 0.45 lbs/day since 2026-09-15 vs 1.0 target'.

findings.regression_test: W-07 data: a serious T6 row 'No reading for 42 hours; last level 98.5%' plus a data issue naming '2026-10-29'. W-06 data: silentHours >= 0 for every tank. Committed data with as_of 2026-09-15T18:00: no Water rows. GN-12 data: Heifers '0.44 lbs/day since 2026-07-20' plus a note of 1 weigh-in after as_of.

Rows after as_of are left out and reported as a data issue. Clamp chart x positions to the plot.

findings.title: No time-zone contract: a date-only as_of, UTC-stamped readings and daylight-saving days make silent hours, the 24-hour drop and the header depend on the viewer's zone
findings.verifier: confirmed (verify_time F4, F10). Evidence: TIME-03 (date-only as_of) gives silentHours 18 (UTC), 13 (Chicago), 12 (Denver) and 31 (Auckland, 'serious: No reading for 31 hours'); TIME-04 (a 'Z' reading) gives 22 / 27 serious / 28 serious / 9; the TIME-01 spring-forward leak is critical in UTC and Auckland but '(no alert)' in Chicago and Denver. Corrections applied: with explicit offsets on both stamps the elapsed hours agree for every viewer, but the calendar-day rules still need the ranch-zone date (TIME-03); on the fall-back day the Chicago answer 'No reading for 24 hours' is physically right, so the defect is the dependence on the viewer, not a wrong Chicago value.
findings.location: exceptions.js:36, :45, :48 (elapsed time from local-time parsing); app.js:223 (header in the viewer's zone, no zone shown); app.js:73 (water window)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/time.repro.mjs (CASE TIME-01, TIME-02, TIME-03, TIME-04; each runs under TZ=UTC, America/Chicago, America/Denver and Pacific/Auckland); node docs/audit/diagnostics/time.browser.mjs (CASE TB-01, TB-08).
findings.expected: The same CSVs give the same alerts for every viewer. With meta 'as_of,timezone' = '2026-09-30T18:00,America/Chicago' and a reading at 2026-09-29T20:00Z, silentHours = 27 in every zone (18:00 CDT = 23:00Z; 23:00Z minus 20:00Z the day before = 27 h). TIME-01: critical 'Dropped 32 points in 24 hours, now 48%' for every viewer. The header shows the zone ('Sep 30, 2026 6:00 PM CDT').
findings.actual: TIME-03: UTC 'silentHours=18; (no alert)'; Chicago 13; Denver 12; Auckland 'silentHours=31; serious: ... No reading for 31 hours'. TIME-04: UTC 22 (no alert); Chicago 27 (serious); Denver 28 (serious); Auckland 9 (no alert). TB-01 header: UTC 'September 30, 2026 at 12:00 AM'; Chicago 'September 29, 2026 at 7:00 PM'. TIME-01: UTC and Auckland critical; Chicago and Denver '(no alert)'.
findings.consequence: The same export gives different alerts depending on whose laptop opens it, and CI runs in UTC, so tests cannot catch what a Central-time viewer sees. Sensor data stamped in UTC misses or invents a silent sensor by the UTC offset, and twice a year a Central viewer can miss a leak.
findings.regression_test: Run one fixture in child processes under TZ=UTC and TZ=America/Chicago: meta as_of 2026-09-30T18:00 with timezone America/Chicago and a reading at 2026-09-29T20:00Z gives silentHours 27 in both. The TIME-01 fixture gives critical 'Dropped 32 points' in both (the maximum in the trailing 24 h is 80; 80 - 48 = 32). A date-only as_of gives a data issue.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a ranch time zone to meta.csv (or require full offsets in exports, and still derive calendar dates in the ranch zone). Read stamps as ranch wall-clock time with Intl and compute elapsed time from those values, never from new Date(string). Show the zone in the header. One as-of policy for the whole page.

findings.title: A UTC-stamped as_of shifts every calendar-day count by one day for evening exports, the same way for every viewer
findings.verifier: confirmed (the time skeptic's own missed finding MISSED-1). Evidence: with meta as_of '2026-10-01T01:00Z' (= Sep 30 20:00 CDT) the output is identical in UTC, Chicago and Auckland: 'Day 25 of a 21-day plan (4 days over)', 'Overdue by 16 days' and two false 'Planned move in 2 days' warnings; the -05:00 control gives the committed rows. Browser (Chicago): header 'September 30, 2026 at 8:00 PM.', 12 rows, '+4d'. Registrar re-ran time.verify.mjs MISSED-1 on 2026-10-16: same.

findings.expected: The ranch calendar date is Sep 30, so the committed rows appear: 'Yearlings in Sand Hills: Day 24 of a 21-day plan (3 days over)', 'Yearlings: Booster vaccine: Overdue by 15 days (due 2026-09-15)', 'Cows: Pinkeye check: Due in 3 days (2026-10-03)', 10 rows, overstay label '+3d'.

Browser (Chicago): 12 rows and '+4d'. Boundary fixture: 'serious: Day 22 of a 21-day plan (1 day over)' and 'serious: Overdue by 1 day (due 2026-09-30)' instead of two warnings at 0 days.
findings.consequence: Exports stamped in UTC after 7 PM Central count from the next day: groups are flagged over plan and health tasks overdue a day early (a warning becomes serious), two false move warnings appear, and the header's 'September 30' contradicts the rows. Testing across viewer zones will not catch it because every viewer gets the same wrong answer.

findings.title: Tank levels are never validated: a fault code ('ERR', 'NaN', '11.8%') hides a critical tank as fine, and a blank, -999 or 140 reading raises a false critical leak
findings.verifier: confirmed (verify_water F1, verify_csv F4, verify_render F6). Evidence: W-10 'level="ERR" drop24h=NaN; (no water alerts)'; B-05 (T2's newest row set to ERR) removes T2's critical row, tile 'WATER TANKS OK 6 of 8 2 need a look', heading 'T2 Windmill ERR%'; W-09 'critical | Tank T1 (North Flat) | Dropped 80 points in 24 hours, now %'; CSV-53 'Dropped 1079 points in 24 hours, now -999%'. Corrections applied: regression test (c) was garbled; T2's last good reading is 14.8 at 2026-09-30T12:00 (data/water.csv line 240). An ERR on the 24-hour baseline row silently disables the leak rule (T4 becomes 'Down to 10% full'). The render skeptic showed any blank latest level gives a critical row because '' < 25 is true ('Down to % full' with a prior level of 28). The CSV skeptic noted high rests on the silent all-clear cases; '-999' and '140' still make someone look. Registrar re-ran water.repro W-09/W-10 and csv.repro CSV-43/51 on 2026-10-16: same.
findings.location: exceptions.js:30 (non-numbers stay strings; 'Infinity' becomes Infinity), :47-49 (level and drop from the last row, unchecked), :109-115 (comparisons against a string or NaN); app.js:47, :55, :82, :91, :93 (tile, heading and SVG from the raw value)

Minimal input: rows 'T1,P1,2026-09-29T18:00,80' and 'T1,P1,2026-09-30T18:00,ERR' with as_of 2026-09-30T18:00.
findings.expected: A reading that is not a finite number from 0 to 100 is not used as a level. The tank is flagged as a sensor or data problem (serious: 'last reading ERR is not a level; last good level 80% at Sep 29 18:00') and counted as needing a look. With T2's newest row set to ERR: a T2 row still appears ('last good level 14.8% at Sep 30 12:00') and the tile reads '5 of 8, 3 need a look'. A blank last level never produces 'now %' or 'Down to % full'.
findings.actual: W-10: 'level="ERR" drop24h=NaN; (no water alerts)'. B-05: T2's critical row disappears; tile 'WATER TANKS OK 6 of 8 2 need a look'; heading 'T2 Windmill ERR%'; console 'Error: <path> attribute d: Expected number, "...45.9,79.6L254.0,NaN".' W-09: 'critical | Tank T1 (North Flat) | Dropped 80 points in 24 hours, now %'. CSV-53: 'critical|Tank T1 (North Flat)|Dropped 1079 points in 24 hours, now -999%'. CSV-54: 'Dropped 40 points in 24 hours, now 100%' for a 140 spike. CSV-50/51/52: '(no alerts)'.
findings.consequence: Fault codes and blanks are common in tank-sensor exports. A fault code on the newest row turns the most urgent tank (T2 at 11.8%) into an all-clear, so nobody goes and cattle can run out of water. A blank or out-of-range last row raises a false critical leak with garbled text and sends a crew to haul water to a full tank.

In waterStatus take level, drop and last-good time from valid rows only. If the newest row is invalid, mark the tank 'unknown' with the bad value and time, emit a serious 'Last reading <v> at <time> is not a level; last good level <L>% at <t>', and count it as needing a look. The chart skips invalid points and says 'bad reading' in the heading.

findings.title: There is no tanks master list: a tank with no readings in the export, or an empty water file, disappears and the page reports water as fine
findings.verifier: design-limitation (verify_water F2, verify_csv F11). Evidence: W-08 (every T6 row removed) gives 'tanks=7' and only the T2 and T4 rows; B-02 tile 'WATER TANKS OK 5 of 7 2 need a look', 7 charts, no T6 anywhere; CSV-29 '(no alerts)'; B-05 (header-only water.csv) tile 'WATER TANKS OK / 0 of 0 / 0 need a look' and 'Water (0)'. scripts/generate_data.py:39 defines TANKS but main() never writes a tanks file. The water skeptic said high is defensible on consequence (a confident all-clear on water) and that likelihood depends on the export shape: a full-period export loses a tank only if it never reported; a rolling-window export or a sensor replaced under a new device ID makes it likely ('consider medium-high'). The registry keeps high because the result is a false all-clear on the most time-critical area. The empty-file case is also listed under LOAD-01.
findings.location: exceptions.js:39-52 (the tank list is built from water rows only); app.js:46, :55, :78 (tile and charts); scripts/generate_data.py:39 (TANKS defined, never written)

findings.expected: 8 tanks, from a tanks master file (tanks.csv). T6 (Cedar Draw) flagged serious 'no readings in this export'; tile 'Water tanks OK 5 of 8, 3 need a look'. A header-only water.csv gives a 'no water readings loaded' state (CAN'T TELL) for all 8 tanks, never '0 of 0'. A tank_id in water.csv that is not in tanks.csv is a data issue.

B-02: tile 'WATER TANKS OK 5 of 7 2 need a look', 7 charts. B-05: tile 'WATER TANKS OK / 0 of 0 / 0 need a look', chips 'Water (0)'.
findings.consequence: The silent-sensor rule only works while the dead sensor's old rows are still in the file. With a rolling export, a replaced sensor or a gateway that exports nothing, a tank nobody is watching vanishes and the page shows a confident all-clear on water.

findings.title: The 24-hour drop is not a 24-hour window: after a reading gap a multi-day change is reported as 'in 24 hours', a new sensor's fast drop is missed, and a fall that refills before the last reading is not seen
findings.verifier: confirmed (verify_water F4, F5; verify_time F7), design-limitation (verify_water F12). Evidence: W-01 'critical | Tank T1 (North Flat) | Dropped 36 points in 24 hours, now 54%' (baseline 72 h old); W-02 'drop24h=0; (no water alerts)' for 95, 80, 65, 50 on one day; TIME-16 'Dropped 32 points in 24 hours, now 48%' across a 4-day gap; W-03 'drop24h=4' after a 90 to 50 fall that refilled. Corrections applied: 'resumed sensor' is wrong for W-02 (a resumed sensor has a pre-gap row and takes the W-01 path); the trigger is a new sensor or an export starting less than 24 h before the last reading. The time skeptic said do not skip the rule when no reading is 18-30 h old; judge max-in-window minus last whenever the window has a reading and add a coverage note. Both skeptics checked the max-in-window rule on the committed data: worst 24-h drawdowns T1 16.1, T2 15.3, T3 16.2, T4 46, T5 14.5, T6 12.4, T7 17.1, T8 18.2, so no new alarm and T4 stays at 46. The daylight-saving variant is in TIME-02. Registrar re-ran W-01/W-02/W-03 and TIME-16 on 2026-10-16: same.
findings.location: exceptions.js:45 (dayAgo = latest row at least 1 day before the last, any age), :49 (endpoint difference only), :110 (hard-coded 'in 24 hours'); app.js:204 and README.md (rule text)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/water.repro.mjs (CASE W-01 gap, W-02 new sensor, W-03 refill); node docs/audit/diagnostics/time.repro.mjs (CASE TIME-16). Minimal input: T1 rows 2026-09-27T12:00 91, 2026-09-27T18:00 90, 2026-09-30T12:00 56, 2026-09-30T18:00 54; as_of 2026-09-30T18:00.
findings.expected: W-01: no water alert (inside the true 24 h the readings are 56 then 54; 54% is above the 40% demo line), or text that states the real span ('36 points over 72 hours'). W-02: critical, 45 points in 18 hours (95 - 50). W-03: the 40-point fall inside the window (90 - 50) reported. Committed data: the same 3 Water rows.
findings.actual: W-01: 'critical | Tank T1 (North Flat) | Dropped 36 points in 24 hours, now 54%'. W-02: 'drop24h=0; (no water alerts)'. W-03: 'drop24h=4; (no water alerts)'. TIME-16: 'critical: Tank T1 (North Flat): Dropped 32 points in 24 hours, now 48%'.
findings.consequence: After a radio outage, a slow decline is reported as a critical overnight leak and a crew is sent to haul water. A brand-new sensor's tank can drain about 2.5 points an hour with no alert. A sticking float that refills before the next reading goes unreported until it fails. The '24 hours' wording in the README and rules table is untrue whenever readings are irregular.
findings.regression_test: W-01 rows: 0 Water rows (window max 56, last 54). W-02 rows: one critical T1 row containing '45 points' and '18 hours'. W-03 rows: one T1 row mentioning 40 points (90 - 50). Contiguous control 2026-09-29T18:00 80 ... 2026-09-30T18:00 48: critical 'Dropped 32 points in 24 hours, now 48%'. Committed data: still exactly 3 Water rows and T4 at 46 points.
findings.proposed_fix: Use only readings in [last.time - 24 h, last.time] in the same pasture placement; drop = max level in that window minus the last level (or the max drawdown inside it); state the real span in hours; when the window holds only the last reading, say the 24-hour change can't be judged rather than reporting 0. The 30-point line stays a demo setting.

findings.title: Water severity uses level percent alone: it ignores stock on the pasture, tank capacity and use, and ties are broken by file order, so an empty-pasture tank outranks a leaking tank 45 heifers drink from
findings.verifier: design-limitation (verify_water F9). Evidence: W-14 lists 'critical | Tank T2 (Windmill) | Down to 11.8% full' before 'critical | Tank T4 (Lone Tree, Heifers here now) | Dropped 46 points in 24 hours, now 10%' although P2 Windmill is empty (open moves put Cows in P7, Heifers in P4, Yearlings in P3); W-16 lists the empty-pasture TB before TA with 180 pairs, both at 38%. Correction applied: T2 comes before T4 only because T2 comes first in water.csv; within a severity the sort has no level or stock key, so the order is file-order chance. The gallons illustration (a 1,000-gal tank at 38% with 180 pairs at about 20 gal per pair per day lasts about 2.5 hours) uses assumed figures that are not in the data. Area-name ordering across areas is UI-09.
findings.location: exceptions.js:109-115 (level and drop thresholds only); exceptions.js:158 (within a severity, order is file order); no capacity or head data in water.csv
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/water.repro.mjs (CASE W-14 committed data; W-16: TA in P7 with Cows here now and TB in empty P2, both at 38%).
findings.expected: Rows where stock is drinking come first or rate higher: on the committed data the first Water row is Tank T4 (Lone Tree, Heifers here now); in W-16, TA ranks or rates above TB.
findings.actual: W-14: 'critical | Tank T2 (Windmill) | Down to 11.8% full || critical | Tank T4 (Lone Tree, Heifers here now) | Dropped 46 points in 24 hours, now 10% || serious | Tank T6 ...'. W-16: 'warning | Tank TB (Windmill) | 38% full || warning | Tank TA (South Divide, Cows here now) | 38% full'.
findings.consequence: The top row of the report sends the crew to an empty pasture while the leaking tank 45 heifers depend on is second. A 38% tank with 180 pairs on it gets 'look at it on the next pass'. The data model cannot say whether water is actually short.
findings.regression_test: Phase 1 (honest copy): the rules table says water severity uses level percent only. Phase 2 (with UI-09's consequence-aware ranking): committed data, the first Water row's subject contains 'Tank T4'; W-16, TA comes before TB. Phase 3: with capacity_gal and a stated gallons-per-head assumption (a demo setting, labelled as such), a 1,000-gal tank at 38% with 180 head at 20 gal/day gives hours left = 380 / (180 x 20 / 24) = 2.53 h by hand.
findings.proposed_fix: Phase 1 (honest copy): state in the rules table that water severity uses level percent only. Phase 2, with UI-09's consequence-aware ranking: rank stocked-pasture water rows first and show the head count in 'here now'. Phase 3 (one of the three allowed additions): water supply coverage from tank capacity and head count, with the gallons-per-head figure labelled as an assumption.

The F4 skeptic confirmed at medium that one blank in_date wipes all 23 bars and silently drops the planted serious alert. findings.location: exceptions.js:30 (text kept as a string), :56 (!m.out_date treats any text as a closed stay), :58 (raw in_date vs as_of date), :119-125 (NaN fails both tests, so no row; a blank plan acts as 0); app.js:113 (start = '' when an in_date is blank), :117-118, :129-131 (NaN bar width)

findings.expected: Each bad cell becomes a Grazing data issue naming the group or pasture and the value ("Yearlings: out_date '-' isn't a date; leave it blank for the current stay"; "No usable plan for Sand Hills"), and the rest is judged as usual: at least 10 rows on otherwise committed data; T4 still reads 'Tank T4 (Lone Tree, Heifers here now)'; the other 22 timeline bars still drawn; never '-day plan' or fractional days.
findings.actual: X-GRZ-a: 'total=9; grazing=[]'. X-GRZ-b: T4 subject 'Tank T4 (Lone Tree)'. X-GRZ-c: 'total=9; grazing=[]'. G-09: '(no rows)  ## grazingStatus days=NaN -> over=NaN'. G-11: '[serious] Yearlings in Sand Hills | Day 24 of a -day plan (24 days over)'. G-10 (TZ=UTC): 'Day 23.75 of a 21-day plan (2.75 days over)'.

One blank date wipes the whole rotation chart.
findings.regression_test: Committed data with as_of 2026-09-30T18:00: (1) Yearlings open row out_date '-': length >= 10 and a Grazing row mentions 'Yearlings' and matches /3 days over|not a date|out_date/i (Sep 6 + 21 = Sep 27). (2) P3 plan '21 days': length >= 10, a Grazing row mentions 'Sand Hills' and /plan/i, and no row matches / -day plan/. findings.proposed_fix: In the data contract: in_date and out_date must be blank (out_date only) or valid YYYY-MM-DD dates; planned_graze_days must be a positive whole number. findings.title: Budget 'season to date' ignores the month column and as_of: future plan rows hide both real overspends, a blank or lagging month changes the total, and a mid-month as_of compares part of a month with a full month's budget
findings.verifier: confirmed (verify_healthbudget F1, verify_time F2), design-limitation (verify_time F14). Evidence: BU-06 / TIME-14 'Fuel 11640/14400 = -19.2%; Repairs 9000/10800 = -16.7%; (no alerts)'; AB-07 / TB-06 tile 'SPEND VS BUDGET −32.7% $89,303 of $132,600'; the skeptic added that as_of is also ignored (as_of 2026-07-31 still gives 'Fuel 21% over season to date ($2,040)'); TIME-D1 (as_of Sep 15, half-month actual) 'warning: Fuel: 6% over season to date'. Corrections applied: 'the normal way to load a budget' overstates it a little; high stands because a full-season plan with future actuals at 0 is a common shape and the result is a silent all-clear; the blank Sep Fuel case belongs here (blank counted as 0), not to the string bug (BUD-02). The time skeptic showed the fix needs a season start bound (2025 rows at 95% of budget are kept by a 'month <= as_of month' filter) and month normalisation ('2026-09-01' <= '2026-09' is false); front-loaded costs make pro-rating risky, so closed months only is the safer default. Registrar re-ran BU-06, AB-07 and TIME-14 on 2026-10-16: same.
findings.location: exceptions.js:82-89 (budgetStatus never reads r.month or as_of), :149-156; app.js:49, :57 (tile totals); README.md:28
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/healthbudget.repro.mjs (CASE BU-06 and AB-07: committed data plus '2026-10,<cat>,<plan>,0' and '2026-11,<cat>,<plan>,0' for all 6 categories; BU-04 and AB-08: Sep Fuel actual blank; BU-07: Sep Fuel row deleted); node docs/audit/diagnostics/time.repro.mjs (CASE TIME-14, TIME-15, TIME-D1); node docs/audit/diagnostics/time.browser.mjs (CASE TB-06, TB-07).
findings.expected: One as-of policy: budget counts closed months from the season start through the last month that closed on or before as_of, and the tile names those months. On the committed data (as_of Sep 30, so Jun-Sep closed): Fuel serious '21% over season to date ($2,040)' (11,640 vs 9,600) and Repairs serious '25% over ($1,800)' (9,000 vs 7,200); tile '+1.0% $89,303 of $88,400'. Future rows change nothing. A blank or missing month for a category is reported as a data issue ('Fuel: 2026-09 actual not entered'), never counted as 0.
findings.actual: BU-06: 'Fuel 11640/14400 = -19.2%; Repairs 9000/10800 = -16.7%; (no alerts)'. AB-07 tile: 'SPEND VS BUDGET −32.7% $89,303 of $132,600, season to date', no budget rows in the report. BU-04: 'Fuel actual="8640" (string) pct=-0.1' and the Fuel alert is gone. BU-07: 'serious | Fuel | 20% over season to date ($1,440)' with no mention that September is missing. TIME-D1: 'warning: Fuel: 6% over season to date'.
findings.consequence: Loading the season's whole plan up front makes both real overspends disappear and tells the manager spending is 32.7% under budget. Bookkeeping that lags a month does the same for that category, and a mid-month review understates overspend.
findings.regression_test: Committed budget.csv plus Oct and Nov rows (budget = monthly plan, actual 0): Budget rows deep-equal [['serious','Fuel','21% over season to date ($2,040)'], ['serious','Repairs','25% over season to date ($1,800)']]; tile '+1.0%' and '$89,303 of $88,400'. Hand sums: Fuel 2592 + 2928 + 3120 + 3000 = 11,640 vs 4 x 2,400 = 9,600; Repairs 9,000 vs 7,200; totals 89,303 vs 4 x 22,100 = 88,400. 2025 rows appended: no change. Months written '2026-09-01': September still counted. Sep Fuel actual blank: a data issue naming 2026-09 and Fuel. TIME-D1 (as_of 2026-09-15): Jun-Aug only, Fuel 8,640 vs 7,200 = 20% over, serious. These values assume a month closes on its last calendar day (see proposed_fix).
findings.proposed_fix: Add a season start to meta.csv; normalise month to YYYY-MM in the data contract; pass as_of into budgetStatus and count only closed months in [season start, last month closed on or before as_of]; treat a blank actual as 'not entered' (data issue) and check each category has every month in range. Show the months covered in the tile and rules copy. A month counts as closed when the ranch-zone as-of date is on or after its last day, so as_of 2026-09-30T18:00 closes September (an assumption, listed in unresolved_assumptions). If the ranch prefers 'closed once the last day has ended', September drops out on Sep 30 and the committed rows read Fuel 20.0% over ($1,440: 8,640 vs 7,200) and Repairs 13.3% over ($720: 6,120 vs 5,400), both still serious.
findings.status_note: The future-rows and ignored-as_of parts are confirmed defects; the mid-month comparison (verify_time F14) is a design limitation resolved by the closed-months policy.

findings.title: Budget boundaries are inconsistent: exactly 5.0% gets no row though the rules say '5-10%', 9.6% and 10.4% both print '10% over' at different severities, and summed cents can tip an exact 10.00% into serious
findings.verifier: confirmed (verify_healthbudget F8, F9). Evidence: BU-08 ('2026-09,X,1000,1050') '(no alerts)'; BU-09 '9.6%: warning | X | 10% over ... ## 10.4%: serious | X | 10% over season to date ($104)'; BU-10 'pct=0.10000000000000007; serious | X | 10% over season to date ($741.9)'. Corrections applied: the README rule text is README.md:28, not :243; 1,051 vs 1,000 prints '5% over' and is flagged while 1,050 prints nothing; the cents case came from a search and needs an overrun of exactly 10.000% to the cent.
findings.location: exceptions.js:86-88 (float sums), :150 (Math.round(pct*100)), :151 (> budgetSerious), :154 (> budgetWarn); app.js:213-214; README.md:28
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/healthbudget.repro.mjs (CASE BU-08, BU-09, BU-10, HB-C7).
findings.expected: Stated, consistent bounds (for example warning at 5% or more up to 10%, serious above 10%), one-decimal percentages so two severities never show the same number, and integer-cent arithmetic so 10.00% is never serious.
findings.actual: BU-08: '(no alerts)'. BU-09: '9.6%: warning | X | 10% over season to date | Watch it next month  ##  10.4%: serious | X | 10% over season to date ($104)'. HB-C7: 'warning | X | 10% over season to date'. BU-10: 'code budget=7419 actual=8160.900000000001 pct=0.10000000000000007; serious | X | 10% over season to date ($741.9)'.
findings.consequence: Two rows that both read '10% over' get different severities and actions, and an exact 5% overrun contradicts the published rule text.
findings.regression_test: 1,050 vs 1,000: warning '5.0% over'. 1,096: warning '9.6% over'. 1,104: serious '10.4% over'. 1,100: warning '10.0% over'. BU-10 rows: warning (integer cents 74,190 x 10 = 741,900).
findings.proposed_fix: Pick and state inclusive bounds; compare in integer cents; print one decimal; make the rules table and README.md:28 match. If one-decimal printing is adopted, update the whole-percent strings quoted in the BUD-01, BUD-02, BUD-07 and DATA-03 tests: Fuel 21.3% (2,040 / 9,600 = 21.25%, rounded half up from integer cents), Repairs 25.0%, BUD-02's Repairs case 20.8% (1,500 / 7,200), BUD-07's rows 50.0% under.
